`split(';')` breaks when SQL string literals contain semicolons\n315\t/// (e.g., `INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('a;b')`). This function uses a small state\n316\t/// machine to track whether the current position is inside:\n317\t/// - A single-quoted string literal (`'...'`, with `''` as escape)\n318\t/// - A double-quoted identifier (`\"...\"`, with `\"\"` as escape)\n319\t/// - A line comment (`-- ...`)\n320\t/// - A block comment (`/* ... */`)\n321\t///\n322\t/// Only semicolons at the top level (outside all of the above) are treated as\n323\t/// statement terminators.\n324\tfn split_sql_statements(sql: &str) -> Vec<&str> {\n325\t    let bytes = sql.as_bytes();\n326\t    let len = bytes.len();\n327\t    let mut stmts = Vec::new();\n328\t    let mut start = 0; // byte offset where the current statement begins\n329\t    let mut i = 0;\n330\t\n331\t    // State flags — at most one is true at a time.\n332\t    let mut in_single_quote = false;\n333\t    let mut in_double_quote = false;\n334\t    let mut in_line_comment = false;\n335\t    let mut in_block_comment = false;\n336\t\n337\t    while i < len {\n338\t        let b = bytes[i];\n339\t\n340\t        // --- Line comment state ---\n341\t        if in_line_comment {\n342\t            if b == b'\\n' {\n343\t                in_line_comment = false;\n344\t            }\n345\t            i += 1;\n346\t            continue;\n347\t        }\n348\t\n349\t        // --- Block comment state ---\n350\t        if in_block_comment {\n351\t            if b == b'*' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'/' {\n352\t                in_block_comment = false;\n353\t                i += 2;\n354\t            } else {\n355\t                i += 1;\n356\t            }\n357\t            continue;\n358\t        }\n359\t\n360\t        // --- Single-quoted string state ---\n361\t        if in_single_quote {\n362\t            if b == b'\\'' {\n363\t                // '' is an escaped quote inside a string literal\n364\t                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\\'' {\n365\t                    i += 2;\n366\t                } else {\n367\t                    in_single_quote = false;\n368\t                    i += 1;\n369\t                }\n370\t            } else {\n371\t                i += 1;\n372\t            }\n373\t            continue;\n374\t        }\n375\t\n376\t        // --- Double-quoted identifier state ---\n377\t        if in_double_quote {\n378\t            if b == b'\"' {\n379\t                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\"' {\n380\t                    i += 2;\n381\t                } else {\n382\t                    in_double_quote = false;\n383\t                    i += 1;\n384\t                }\n385\t            } else {\n386\t                i += 1;\n387\t            }\n388\t            continue;\n389\t        }\n390\t\n391\t        // --- Top-level parsing ---\n392\t        if b == b'\\'' {\n393\t            in_single_quote = true;\n394\t            i += 1;\n395\t        } else if b == b'\"' {\n396\t            in_double_quote = true;\n397\t            i += 1;\n398\t        } else if b == b'-' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'-' {\n399\t            in_line_comment = true;\n400\t            i += 2;\n401\t        } else if b == b'/' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'*' {\n402\t            in_block_comment = true;\n403\t            i += 2;\n404\t        } else if b == b';' {\n405\t            // Statement terminator at top level.\n406\t            let stmt = &sql[start..i];\n407\t            if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n408\t                stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n409\t            }\n410\t            start = i + 1;\n411\t            i += 1;\n412\t        } else {\n413\t            i += 1;\n414\t        }\n415\t    }\n416\t\n417\t    // Trailing statement without a final semicolon.\n418\t    if start < len {\n419\t        let stmt = &sql[start..len];\n420\t        if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n421\t            stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n422\t        }\n423\t    }\n424\t\n425\t    stmts\n426\t}\n427\t\n428\t/// Execute multiple SQL statements separated by semicolons.\n429\tfn execute_batch(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n430\t    conn.execute_batch(sql)?;\n431\t    Ok(())\n432\t}\n433\t\n434\tpub fn apply_schema(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n435\t    execute_batch(conn, SCHEMA_SQL)?;\n436\t    apply_migrations(conn)?;\n437\t    Ok(())\n438\t}\n439\t\n440\t/// Apply database migrations for schema changes.\n441\t/// This handles adding new columns to existing tables.\n442\tfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n443\t    // Migration 1: Update critical_path_cache schema if it has the old format\n444\t    // Old format: bead_id, float (REAL), updated_at\n445\t    // New format: bead_id, INTEGER\", [])?;\n501\t    }\n502\t\n503\t    Ok(())\n504\t}\n505\t\n506\tpub fn ensure_wal_mode(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n507\t    // Use execute_batch so PRAGMAs that return rows identifiers, and comments.\n///\n/// A naive `split(';')` breaks when SQL string literals contain semicolons\n/// (e.g., `INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('a;b')`). This function uses a small state\n/// machine to track whether the current position is inside:\n/// - A single-quoted string literal (`'...'`, with `''` as escape)\n/// - A double-quoted identifier (`\"...\"`, with `\"\"` as escape)\n/// - A line comment (`-- ...`)\n/// - A block comment (`/* ... */`)\n///\n/// Only semicolons at the top level (outside all of the above) are treated as\n/// statement terminators.\nfn split_sql_statements(sql: &str) -> Vec<&str> {\n    let bytes = sql.as_bytes();\n    let len = bytes.len();\n    let mut stmts = Vec::new();\n    let mut start = 0; // byte offset where the current statement begins\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    // State flags — at most one is true at a time.\n    let mut in_single_quote = false;\n    let mut in_double_quote = false;\n    let mut in_line_comment = false;\n    let mut in_block_comment = false;\n\n    while i < len {\n        let b = bytes[i];\n\n        // --- Line comment state ---\n        if in_line_comment {\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                in_line_comment = false;\n            }\n            i += 1;\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Block comment state ---\n        if in_block_comment {\n            if b == b'*' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'/' {\n                in_block_comment = false;\n                i += 2;\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Single-quoted string state ---\n        if in_single_quote {\n            if b == b'\\'' {\n                // '' is an escaped quote inside a string literal\n                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\\'' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    in_single_quote = false;\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Double-quoted identifier state ---\n        if in_double_quote {\n            if b == b'\"' {\n                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\"' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    in_double_quote = false;\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Top-level parsing ---\n        if b == b'\\'' {\n            in_single_quote = true;\n            i += 1;\n        } else if b == b'\"' {\n            in_double_quote = true;\n            i += 1;\n        } else if b == b'-' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'-' {\n            in_line_comment = true;\n            i += 2;\n        } else if b == b'/' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'*' {\n            in_block_comment = true;\n            i += 2;\n        } else if b == b';' {\n            // Statement terminator at top level.\n            let stmt = &sql[start..i];\n            if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n                stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n            }\n            start = i + 1;\n            i += 1;\n        } else {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Trailing statement without a final semicolon.\n    if start < len {\n        let stmt = &sql[start..len];\n        if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n            stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n        }\n    }\n\n    stmts\n}\n\n/// Execute multiple SQL statements separated by semicolons.\nfn execute_batch(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    conn.execute_batch(sql)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub fn apply_schema(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    execute_batch(conn, SCHEMA_SQL)?;\n    apply_migrations(conn)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Apply database migrations for schema changes.\n/// This handles adding new columns to existing tables.\nfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    // Migration 1: Update critical_path_cache schema if it has the old format\n    // Old format: bead_id, float (REAL), updated_at\n    // New format: bead_id, epic_id, es (INTEGER), ls (INTEGER), float (INTEGER), updated_at\n    let has_es: bool = conn.query_row(\n        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM critical_path_cache;\n             ALTER TABLE critical_path_cache_new RENAME TO critical_path_cache;\n             COMMIT;\"\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    // Create indexes for critical_path_cache (idempotent)\n    let _ = conn.execute_batch(\n        \"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_critical_path_cache_epic ON critical_path_cache(epic_id);\n         CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_critical_path_cache_float ON critical_path_cache(float);\"\n    );\n\n    // Migration 2: Add workspace_path to worker_sessions if missing\n    // Older databases may not have this column; br conn.execute(\"ALTER TABLE worker_sessions ADD COLUMN closed_at DATETIME\", [])?;\n        conn.execute(\"ALTER TABLE worker_sessions ADD COLUMN duration_seconds INTEGER\", [])?;\n    }\n\n Worker performance tracking and velocity-aware claim scoring.\n//!\n//! This module tracks how long workers take to complete beads based on their\n//! (model, harness, issue_type) configuration and uses this data to inform\n//! claim scoring.\n//!\n//! ## Data Flow\n//!\n//! 1. When a bead is claimed, `worker_sessions` row is created (in claim.rs)\n//! 2. When a bead is closed, the session is updated with `closed_at` and `duration_seconds`\n//! 3. Velocity stats are recomputed from the last 50 sessions per (model, harness, issue_type)\n//! 4. Claim scoring uses expected_seconds from velocity_stats: score = impact / expected_seconds\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse rusqlite::{params, Connection};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\n/// Velocity statistics for a (model, harness, issue_type) tuple.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct VelocityStats {\n    pub model: String,\n    pub harness: String,\n    pub issue_type: String,\n    pub sample_count: i64,\n    pub p50_seconds: Option<i64>,\n    pub p90_seconds: Option<i64>,\n    pub avg_seconds: Option<f64>,\n    pub last_updated: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Worker session record from worker_sessions table.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct WorkerSession {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    pub harness: Option<String>,\n    pub harness_version: Option<String>,\n    pub claimed_at: String,\n    pub bead_id: Option<String>,\n    pub workspace_path: String,\n    pub closed_at: Option<String>,\n    pub duration_seconds: Option<i64>,\n}\n\n/// Update a worker session with close time and duration.\n///\n/// Called when a bead is closed. Finds the most recent claim session for the bead\n/// and updates it with closed_at and duration_seconds.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `tx` - The transaction to use\n/// * `bead_id` - The bead that was closed\n/// * `closed_at` - When the bead was closed\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(true)` if a session was found and updated\n/// * `Ok(false)` if no matching session was found\npub fn update_session_on_close(\n    tx: &Connection,\n    bead_id: &str,\n    closed_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n) -> Result<bool> {\n    // Find the most recent session for this bead\n    let (claimed_at_str, model, harness, issue_type): (String, Option<String>, Option<String>, Option<String>) =\n        tx.query_row(\n            \"SELECT ws.claimed_at, ws.model, ws.harness, i.issue_type\n             FROM worker_sessions ws\n             INNER JOIN issues i ON i.id = ws.bead_id\n             WHERE ws.bead_id = ?1\n             ORDER BY ws.claimed_at DESC\n             LIMIT 1\",\n            params![bead_id],\n            |row| {\n                let claimed_at: String = row.get(0)?;\n                let model: Option<String> = row.get(1)?;\n                let harness: Option<String> = row.get(2)?;\n                let issue_type: Option<String> = row.get(3)?;\n                Ok((claimed_at, model, harness, issue_type))\n            },\n        )?;\n\n    // Parse claimed_at and Ok(false)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Recompute velocity statistics for a given (model, harness, issue_type) tuple.\n///\n/// Queries the last 50 completed sessions for the tuple and computes\n/// p50, p90, and recompute_velocity_stats(\n    tx: &Connection,\n    model: &str,\n    harness: &str,\n    issue_type: &str,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Get last 50 completed sessions for this tuple\n    let mut stmt .query_map(params![model, harness, issue_type], |row| row.get(0))?\n        .collect::<std::result::Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;\n\n    let sample_count = durations.len() as i64;\n    let (p50_seconds, percentiles\n        let p50_idx = (len as f64 * 0.5).floor() as usize;\n        let p90_idx = (len as f64 * 0.9).floor() as usize;\n        let p50 = Some(durations[p50_idx]);\n        let p90 = if This was removed because:\n477-\n478-1. **SQLite is sufficient**: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` provides serialized write access. Claim latency is ~0.5-2ms — 4-16× faster than the previous flock+streaming-rewrite approach.\n479-2. **Simpler operations**: No flock infrastructure, no streaming rewrite, no temp files during normal operation. All mutation logic is SQL.\n480-3. **Crash recovery is automatic**: SQLite rolls back incomplete transactions on next open.
